narrative.northStar: 法典与台账 (The Statute Book and Its Register)
narrative.overview: The site performs its own deliverable: a legal capability catalog typeset with the discipline of a statute register, where a buyer audits capabilities the way they would audit a legal document. The world is a cool, quiet archive: a statute-navy field opens and closes the page (hero, footer), between them sections sit on cool paper. Depth comes from rules, not shadows — 1px hairlines and 2px strong rules organize every list into a ledger. There is exactly one ornament with a license: the seal vermilion, which appears in two meanings only — the brand seal, and the truthful "on-prem only" marking whose visibility is the point.
keyCharacteristics: Statute-navy owns whole regions; body sections stay on cool paper — never scatter navy accents.
Ledger rows with ruled borders instead of card grids.
Seal vermilion: brand seal + honest limitation marks, nothing else.
One authored motion moment (hero reveal); otherwise static and calm.

rules.name: The Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: Vermilion appears only as the seal or as an on-prem-only annotation. If vermilion shows up for decoration, the annotation has lost its voice.

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: Navy is a field color (hero, footer, primary button fill), never a text accent inside body sections.

rules.name: The Flat Doctrine
rules.body: Zero shadows; structure comes from 2px ink register bounds and 1px hairline row rules. Hover changes color, never elevation.

dos: Do keep body line-length near 36 CJK characters (max-w-[36rem]) and line-height 1.8.
Do bound registers with a 2px ink rule and divide rows with 1px hairline.
Do restate both languages with identical key structure — the site is bilingual by contract.
Do mark every capability's host availability honestly; limitations in vermilion.
donts: Don't use shadows, gradients, or glass for depth; use rules and tonal fields.
Don't introduce icon fonts or emoji; draw the few glyphs as SVG.
Don't publish price numbers, hardware specs, or contact endpoints — quote-on-request chips and labeled placeholders only.
Don't animate beyond the hero reveal; the register stays still.
